ecus.name: Body control module / body zone controller
ecus.function: Switches and protects body loads (exterior and interior lamps, locks, wipers, heaters, horn, window and seat motors in some architectures) through smart high-side / low-side switches and motor drivers, reads switches, and talks CAN / CAN FD / LIN (and 100BASE-T1 on zonal designs). In zonal architectures it also distributes power as an electronic fuse box.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: not published in any source found
pcb.technology: Production example: Tesla Model 3 body controllers act as both fuse boxes and body controllers with no fuses, relying on MOSFETs and current detection for protection (Ingineerix teardown as reported by Jalopnik). Other facts: not published in any source found.
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: Tesla Model 3 splits body control across three controllers: VCFRONT (behind the frunk), VCLEFT and VCRIGHT (footwells), each controlling the loads near it (Jalopnik on the Ingineerix teardown). VW ID.3: Continental ICAS1 server absorbs the former gateway and comprehensive body-domain functions (Continental, eeNews Europe). Board count of a conventional BCM: not published in any source found.

notes: No public board or module cost figure was found for any body / comfort board (searched English and Chinese; results were aftermarket resale and repair prices, which are not production costs and are not recorded).

No production teardown naming chips was found for a BCM (beyond Tesla Model 3: Tesla ASICs + ST Power Architecture MCU, EE Times), gateway, seat, door, HVAC or headlamp module. Layer count, size and laminate are unpublished for all six boards.
VW ID.3 ICAS1: the Renesas R-Car M3 + RH850 claim comes from a fan wiki (meinid.com/wiki/entry/17-icas1/) and is not used as evidence; Continental declined to name the processor.
The task's TIDA-00296 parts list does not include a DRV motor driver or a TCAN transceiver (TI tool page).
Seat, HVAC and part of the door / BCM MCU rows say 'engineering judgement': no source found names the production MCU for these modules; the parts listed come from the library task file.
